entry.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella Calls Xbox Layoffs 'Streamlining'
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Microsoft has cut at least 5,750 jobs through five rounds of layoffs since the October 2023 acquisition of Activision Blizzard, a process CEO Satya Nadella has characterized as "streamlining" the Xbox division. The most recent round, confirmed in July 2026, involves 3,200 roles within Xbox Game Studios and includes the divestment of studios such as Double Fine, Compulsion Games, and Undead Labs.

This restructuring follows a leadership transition to new Xbox head Asha Sharma and occurs amidst declining hardware revenue and a component shortage driven by AI datacenter demand. While Nadella expressed confidence in the company's intellectual property and projected growth for the upcoming fiscal year, affected developers have warned that the loss of specialized talent could disrupt complex production pipelines.

entry.title: Steam Beta Introduces Pyrowave Experimental Video Codec for Low-Latency Streaming
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | phoronix.com | source | discussion

Valve has added Pyrowave, an experimental video codec, to the Steam client beta for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Developed by Hans-Kristian Arntzen, the codec is designed for high-bandwidth, low-latency video streaming, specifically targeting local network usage over Gigabit Ethernet.

Pyrowave utilizes the Vulkan API and supports HDR and YUV 4:4:4 color formats. Because it requires 5 to 10 times more bandwidth than existing streaming codecs, it is optimized for high-performance LAN environments. The feature is accessible through the Steam Remote Play advanced client settings in the beta versions.

entry.title: Rustunit Removes Swift Package Dependencies from Bevy iOS Crates
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | rustunit.com | discussion

Rustunit has updated its `bevy_ios_*` crates to replace manual Swift package dependencies with direct `objc2` bindings. This allows developers to install necessary iOS functionality, such as safe area insets and user notifications, using only `cargo add`, removing the requirement for the Swift Package Manager (SPM).

This transition simplifies version management between Rust crates and SPM packages and enables builds for the iOS simulator. While most functionality now uses the Objective-C runtime via `objc2`, `bevy_ios_iap` utilizes a minimal, statically linked Swift shim to accommodate the Swift-only StoreKit 2 API.

entry.title: Sam Carlisle Discusses Co-development and Outsourcing in the Game Industry
entry.content:
GDC Videos | youtube.com

Co-development differs from traditional outsourcing in how external partners integrate into a studio's workflow. While traditional outsourcing typically operates on a "time and materials" basis for specific assets, co-development involves partners working directly within a studio's engine and version control systems, granting them greater ownership of the production process.

This model enables studios to scale production and absorb economic volatility while protecting core internal teams from layoffs. Successful external collaboration depends heavily on prioritizing transparent communication and personal relationships over technical ability alone.

entry.title: Wube Software Releases 3D Printable Factorio Models
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | factorio.com | hacker news

Wube Software has released a collection of 247 STL files featuring 65 different 3D models of Factorio entities for fans to print. Developed in collaboration with Prusa Research, the set includes transport belts, machines, enemies, and other early-game elements designed for both push-fit assembly and high-clearance printing.

Instead of selling limited physical collector's items, the developers opted to distribute the digital files for free to encourage community creativity and provide wider accessibility. The models are specifically optimized for FDM printing, with versions designed to minimize the need for support structures.

entry.title: Paranoia-Sans Typeface Automatically Redacts Conspiracy Terms
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | github.com | discussion

This typeface uses OpenType ligatures to automatically redact terms associated with conspiracy theories. By replacing keywords like "5G" with a black box graphic, the font simulates the visual appearance of redacted documents.

Developed by Florian Egermann and based on Courier Prime Sans, the project serves as a satirical exploration of the visual aesthetics of conspiracy myths. The open-source typeface aims to mirror the absurdity of the subjects it redacts through its automated functionality.

entry.title: King Signs Collective Bargaining Agreement with Swedish Unions
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

King has signed a collective bargaining agreement with the Swedish unions Engineers of Sweden and Unionen, preventing a strike that was scheduled to begin on September 25, 2026. The agreement concludes negotiations between the Microsoft subsidiary and its unionized workforce that had been ongoing since May 2025.

The deal grants employees in Malmo and Stockholm more influence over their working conditions and the right to receive timely information regarding workplace changes, such as reorganizations or layoffs. The agreement covers approximately 100 employees across King's Swedish offices.

entry.title: Irish Games Fund Expands with New Funding Strands
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

The Irish Game Makers Association (IMIRT) and Screen Ireland Digital Games Portfolio have expanded the Irish Games Fund for 2026, introducing three distinct funding pathways: a Development Fund, a Prototype Fund, and a Release Fund. The currently active Development Fund offers €50,000 to four teams to assist in transitioning validated concepts and prototypes into full production.

Eligible applicants must be registered Irish studios with at least one year of operation, a history of filed accounts, or previously released commercial projects. The fund has implemented strict guidelines regarding generative AI, stating it will not support projects that plan to use machine learning-generated art, audio, or writing in their final commercial releases due to ongoing intellectual property and copyright risks.

entry.title: Meta Announces AI-Powered Tools for Creating Horizon Games
entry.content:
Techmeme | theverge.com | source

Meta has announced Horizon Create and Horizon Studio, two new AI-powered development tools that allow users to build 2D and 3D games using text prompts. Horizon Create operates as a mobile app, while Horizon Studio is a web-based tool that provides more granular design controls.

To increase reach, Meta intends to host playable versions of these games directly within Facebook and Instagram feeds. This initiative reflects a strategic pivot toward mobile platforms and follows similar AI-assisted development trends in the gaming industry, most notably from Roblox.

entry.title: Google Photos Launches AI-Powered Virtual Closet Feature
entry.content:
TechCrunch AI | techcrunch.com | source

This feature, available to Android and iOS users in the U.S., Brazil, and India, uses artificial intelligence to scan photos and catalog clothing into a digital wardrobe. Users can then filter items by category and mix and match outfits within the app.

The rollout includes several other updates, such as the Gemini Spark prompt-based photo editing tool and an upgraded Markup tool for redacting sensitive information. Google has stated that clothing data used for the feature is not shared with third-party retailers.
